DELTA_R2_VERDICT: The ordering does not hold under the other structure-aware protocol. Under the Butina leave-clusters-out split it reverses: mean-pooled polyBERT reaches 0.563 against 0.438 for ECFP4. A difference that changes sign when the partition is built by chemical similarity rather than by scaffold cannot support a general statement about the two representations, however tight the confidence interval is on any one protocol. We therefore withdraw the claim: what the data show is that the ranking of these two representations is protocol-dependent, not that either generalises better. The abstract, discussion and conclusions have been rewritten accordingly.
DELTA_R2_VERDICT_SHORT: the ordering reverses under the leave-clusters-out protocol (0.563 for polyBERT against 0.438 for ECFP4), so the ranking is protocol-dependent and the original claim is withdrawn.

CONFORMAL_VERDICT: Coverage falls short of nominal by up to 8 percentage points. This is a property of the evaluation design rather than an implementation fault: split conformal guarantees marginal coverage only when the calibration and test partitions are exchangeable, and a scaffold split is constructed precisely so that they are not. The platform therefore reports these intervals with their measured coverage attached rather than with their nominal level, and a user should read an interval labelled 80\% as the empirically 62-to-82\% interval that it is.
CASE_VERDICT: The difference in reliability between successful and failed selections is not statistically resolvable at this sample size, so the index should be read as a guide to expected error magnitude rather than as a per-candidate success probability.
